title: Maximal smooth open of an algebraic stack and flat base change
statement: Schemes and algebraic spaces are as in [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. An algebraic stack is a category fibred in groupoids on schemes, with effective etale descent for objects and sheaf descent for isomorphisms, whose diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces and which has a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Representable means that every scheme-valued 2-base change is an algebraic space. An open substack is a full substack whose pullback by every scheme-valued object is an open subscheme. Smoothness, flatness and local finite presentation of morphisms to schemes are tested after smooth scheme atlases of the source, using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:\mathcal X\to S$ an algebraic stack over it. There exists a largest open substack $\mathcal U_f\subseteq\mathcal X$ such that $f|_{\mathcal U_f}$ is smooth. If $f$ is locally of finite presentation and $g:S'\to S$ is flat, then, for $f':\mathcal X\times_SS'\to S'$, one has $\mathcal U_{f'}=\mathcal U_f\times_SS'$. The fibre product is the 2-fibre product: its objects are pairs of objects together with an isomorphism of their images, and its arrows are pairs compatible with that isomorphism. Scheme fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:P\to\mathcal X$, and put $h=f\circ p$ and $R=P\times_{\mathcal X}P$, with projections $s,t:R\to P$. The presentation in [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent] gives this algebraic space $R$. Both projections are smooth, being base changes of $p$ by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-maximal-smooth-open] to $h:P\to S$, with no flatness or finite-presentation assumption, obtaining its largest smooth open $W\subseteq P$.

source.place: Tag 0DZR (lemma-where-smooth), first paragraph, with target atlas the identity of S.

proof.text: For $r\in|R|$, [lem-sfb-space-smooth-source-point-locality] applied to $s$ gives $s(r)\in W$ if and only if $h\circ s$ is smooth at $r$: membership in $W$ means smoothness on a neighbourhood, by its maximality. The same statement holds for $t$. The isomorphism $p\circ s\simeq p\circ t$ makes the two composites to the scheme $S$ equal. Thus $s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$ as open subspaces. By [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent], $W$ descends to an open substack $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal X$ with $P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U=W$.

source.place: Tag 0DZR (lemma-where-smooth), invariant atlas open; stacks-properties.tex Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation).

proof.text: The map $W\to\mathcal U$ is a smooth surjective scheme atlas by base change of $p$, using [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], and its composite $h|_W$ to $S$ is smooth. The atlas test in the statement, read for every smooth scheme atlas, follows from one atlas: let $Q_1,Q_2$ be smooth surjective scheme atlases of an algebraic stack $\mathcal Z$ over $S$ with $Q_1\to S$ smooth. Then $Q_{12}=Q_1\times_{\mathcal Z}Q_2$ is an algebraic space, smooth and surjective over $Q_1$ and over $Q_2$ by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. By [lem-sfb-space-smooth-source-point-locality], $Q_{12}\to S$ is smooth at every point, and, since every point of $Q_2$ is the image of a point of $Q_{12}$, $Q_2\to S$ is smooth at every point, hence smooth by source locality on the open cover. Thus $f|_{\mathcal U}$ is smooth. If $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal X$ is another smooth open, its atlas $P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal V$, an open of $P$, therefore has smooth composite to $S$. Maximality of $W$ puts this open inside $W$, and the inclusion-preserving correspondence of [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent] gives $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal U$. Therefore $\mathcal U=\mathcal U_f$.

source.place: Tag 0DZR (lemma-where-smooth), maximality paragraph, using the smooth-atlas definition.

proof.text: Now suppose $f$ is locally of finite presentation and $g:S^\prime\to S$ is flat. The pullback stack $\mathcal X^\prime$ is algebraic: triples in its 2-fibre product descend componentwise, its diagonal is the pullback of that of $\mathcal X$, and $P^\prime=P\times_SS^\prime\to\mathcal X^\prime$ is a smooth surjective scheme atlas by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The atlas definition of local finite presentation makes $h:P\to S$ locally of finite presentation. By the flat-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-maximal-smooth-open], the largest smooth open of $h^\prime:P^\prime\to S^\prime$ is $W^\prime=W\times_SS^\prime$. Applying steps 1--3 to $p^\prime$ shows that $\mathcal U_{f^\prime}$ pulls back to $W^\prime$. But the open $\mathcal U_f\times_SS^\prime$ also pulls back to $W^\prime$, by associativity of the defining triples in the 2-fibre product. The injective atlas-open correspondence of [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent] identifies these two open substacks. This is the required equality, without assuming that $g$ is surjective or locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 0DZR (lemma-where-smooth), clause (3) and final proof paragraph, via spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0DZI clause (2).
